**About Sesame**

Sesame believes in a future where computers are lifelike - with the ability to see, hear, and collaborate with us in ways that feel natural and human. With this vision, we're designing a new kind of computer, focused on making voice agents part of our daily lives. Our team brings together founders from Oculus and Ubiquity6, alongside proven leaders from Meta, Google, and Apple, with deep expertise spanning hardware and software. Join us in shaping a future where computers truly come alive.

**About the Role**

We're building smart wearables where the speaker gets a fraction of a cubic centimeter and has to be loud at the ear and quiet to everyone around you. We're looking for a Speaker Systems Engineer to own the speaker system in our products end to end: choosing and specifying the transducers, designing the acoustic path around them in very little space, setting their limits and protection, partnering with the Audio Lead on tuning, and getting them built and tested at volume.

**Responsibilities:**

* Own the speaker path of a shipping consumer electronics product, from transducer selection through enclosure design and factory test
* Translate product-level requirements into speaker system and transducer requirements: bandwidth, level, distortion, leakage, and power budget in the volume available.
* Select, specify, and qualify speakers with suppliers, including evaluation of new and unconventional transducer technologies where they fit the product better than a conventional driver.
* Design and simulate the acoustic path: back volume, ports and leaks, front acoustics, open-ear leakage control, mesh and sealing, in close partnership with mechanical and industrial design.
* Build and measure prototypes; characterize frequency response, distortion, maximum output, far-field leakage, and excursion and thermal limits, and turn the results into design changes and better models.
* Own speaker limits and protection parameters; partner with the Audio Lead on tuning and with firmware on implementation.
* Work with the audio DSP team to minimize speaker-to-mic coupling through the frame.
* Qualify the speaker system for reliability: sweat and ingress, temperature and humidity, drop, mesh clogging, and drift over life.
* Set up and maintain speaker measurement methods in the lab and at the factory, including golden units, limits, and end-of-line acoustic test.
* Support builds and factory ramps, root-cause acoustic yield and quality issues, and drive fixes with suppliers and the CM.
* Work with the cross-functional team (EE, ME, FW, PD) to trade off acoustic performance against size, cost, and power.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Acoustics, Physics, or similar.

* 5+ years of experience integrating speakers into consumer electronics hardware, with at least one shipped product where you owned the speaker system.
* Strong grounding in electroacoustics: lumped-parameter modeling, Thiele/Small parameters, enclosure and port design, and the behavior of small drivers at their limits.
* Hands-on experience specifying and qualifying miniature speakers with transducer suppliers.
* Extensive experience with audio test systems (e.g., SoundCheck, Klippel, Audio Precision) and with measuring distortion, maximum SPL, and rub-and-buzz.
* A record of using acoustic simulation (lumped-parameter and FEM, e.g., COMSOL) to make design decisions, checked against measured hardware.
* Working knowledge of speaker tuning and protection (EQ, limiting, excursion and thermal protection) and how to partner with a DSP team on it.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Masters or Ph.D. in EE, ME, Acoustics, or related disciplines.
* 8+ years of experience in speaker or transducer development for consumer electronics.
* Experience with wearables, hearables, or other products where the speaker sits close to the ear and the acoustic volume is measured in fractions of a cubic centimeter, including open-ear designs.
* Hands-on experience with a range of transducer technologies beyond conventional moving-coil drivers, and a view on where each one fits.
* Transducer design experience: motor, diaphragm, and suspension design, or close work with a supplier’s design team.
* Proficiency in a high-level programming language (e.g., MATLAB, Python) for measurement automation and analysis.
* Familiarity with human perception of sound and psychoacoustic evaluation of speech quality and intelligibility.
* Experience with factory acoustic test development and yield analysis at a contract manufacturer.

Benefits do not apply to contingent/contract workers.

Compensation Range: $175K - $280K

jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

jobs.title: Sr. Program Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
### **Description**

Astrolab is The Lunar Operations Company. We design and build the systems and hardware the lunar economy will come to depend on — rovers, power, and data networks for sustained operations on the Moon. We are focused on the problems that must be solved before the next chapter of human exploration can scale. The Moon does not forgive untested assumptions. The people who work here know that, and they wouldn't have it any other way.  
  
The LTVS Sr. Program System Engineer will be responsible for the integration of the Lunar Terrain Vehicle System (LTVS) project systems and interfaces across all mission phases to ensure the product and systems meet customer (NASA Moon Base and LTV Project) needs and mission objectives. You will report to the LTV Deputy Program Manager (Technical) as a member of the System Engineering and Integration (SEI) team and will collaborate with Responsible Engineers across the program.

### **What you'll do:**

  

* Integration of Program elements (vehicle, delivery system, NASA, ground systems) for program requirements and objectives, including negotiation with customer (NASA) on requirements and deliverables
* Execute program-level trade studies for technical and programmatic considerations affecting vehicle hardware and software design, mission planning, and ground systems
* Collaboration with integrators from Mission Operations, software, and Engineering to ensure consistency across specific mission phases: Lunar transit, Lander deployment and egress, Initial checkouts and first lunar day, Hibernation, and Crewed campaign. This includes collaboration with NASA counterparts for joint definitions
* Ownership or review of scenario-based analysis for technical resources (power/energy, data volume) and surface productivity
* Develop, coordinate, and execute Verification and Validation (V&V) activities for integrated system tests, interface tests with external elements (lander, suits)
* Identify, quantify, and mitigate phase-level program risks
  

  

### **What you'll bring:**

**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in a science, technology, engineering, mathematics (STEM) field
* 5+ years of experience with spacecraft telecommunications, Guidance Navigation & Control (GNC), power, and flight software systems
* Experience with cross-functional engineering projects involving multiple technical disciplines and subject matter experts
* Experience with developing and executing verification and validation (V&V) plans, conducting system-level trade studies, developing requirements, and managing risks, including proficiency with at least one requirements management system

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with robotic systems, particularly rovers, or human-rated spacecraft
* Experience with spacecraft systems in both development and operations
* Spacecraft operations experience, particularly developing early operations and checkout activities
* Hardware-in-the-loop testing experience at the subsystem or system level
* Prior ownership and delivery of major systems engineering products, including design reviews, V&V plans, requirements closure, or system-level analyses
* In-depth technical expertise in at least one spacecraft subsystem, preferably two
* Experience with statistical analysis, such as Monte Carlo simulations
* Experience with Python and MATLAB

  

### **Benefits and Perks**

  

* Join a team of best-in-class engineers building the foundation of planetary surface exploration
* Equity ownership in the company
* Comprehensive health benefits, including medical, dental, vision, and mental health support
* 401(k) plan with company match
* Flexible PTO and parental leave
* Weekly lunch stipend, plus complimentary snacks and beverages on-site
* Once a month social hour on-site with food and drinks

  

### **About Astrolab**

Having a strong, inclusive, and inspired team is essential to accomplishing our bold mission. Employees are our biggest asset, and we are deeply committed to them and our values. At Astrolab we…

**Demonstrate and inspire trust.** Interactions are direct, honest, and respectful. We are fair and transparent with what we do and why.

**Thrive in balance.** Balance gives us perspective and keeps us motivated and inspired. We commit to rewarding work and a fulfilling personal life.

**Seek diverse perspectives.** We ask questions, engage in productive debate and offer alternatives to ensure our solutions and products are robust and a reflection of our collective best.

**Move with purpose.** Quality and reliability are accomplished through efficient ideation and iteration. We act with a sense of urgency and deliver what we promise, always with the big picture in mind.

**Make an impact.** We intentionally move our community and industry into the future through our work, practices, and actions.

---------------

Amazon Web Services' Hardware Engineering team is looking for experienced professionals to help build the world's premier cloud computing platform. The Manufacturing Automation Design & Engineering team designs, validates, and deploys automation solutions, including robotics, cobots, vision inspection, AI-powered quality systems, and automated assembly workflows, across contract manufacturer sites worldwide.  
  
About the Role: You will define the controls and electrical systems architecture for all automated assembly lines, creating the standard control platform that scales across all platforms and all contract manufacturer sites. You own PLC programming standards, HMI development frameworks, safety system architecture, and industrial network design. You define how automated cells communicate with each other, with MES, and with data collection systems. You are the architect of the nervous system that connects every robot, sensor, actuator, and inspection system into a coordinated, data-generating production line. You establish reusable control system templates that ensure consistency and reduce deployment time globally.  
  
The scope covers all server and rack assembly across all architectures and platforms, including compute, AI/ML accelerators, storage, and networking. The team designs intelligent, predictive-analytics-driven production systems where every station is sensor-driven, AI-optimized, and self-correcting, turning assembly lines into programmable, data-generating platforms that scale capacity without scaling headcount. This role requires the engineer to operate in a fast-paced, multi-platform international manufacturing environment with travel to contract manufacturer sites (up to 25-30% travel anticipated).  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Define controls systems architecture: PLC programming standards, HMI frameworks, safety system design, network topology
* Design and program PLC-based control systems for automated assembly lines
* Develop standardized HMI interfaces for operator interaction and production monitoring
* Architect industrial network infrastructure (e.g., EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, EtherCAT) for automated lines
* Design safety system architecture per ISO 13849 and IEC 62443 (functional safety and cybersecurity)
* Create reusable control system templates and code libraries for global deployment standardization
* Define MES integration specifications and data exchange protocols between automation cells and enterprise systems
* Lead controls architecture reviews for automation projects and vendor-supplied systems

The team is responsible for engineering, defining automated process requirements, designing and proving solutions at proof-of-concept, and maintaining AWS-owned intellectual property that scales globally. jobs.title: Software Engineer, AI Kernels & Performance Optimization — MTIA Software
jobs.description:
Meta designs and deploys its own AI systems. MTIA — the Meta Training and Inference Accelerator — is Meta's family of in-house AI accelerator ASICs, running recommendation and ranking workloads in production across Meta's data centers today and expanding into generative AI inference and training as successive silicon generations land (see [https://bit.ly/metamtia](https://bit.ly/metamtia)).The MTIA Software team is part of the \*\*AI & Compute Foundation (ACF)\*\* organization within Meta Infrastructure. Because the hardware is ours, the software is ours too: we build the entire stack a chip vendor would normally supply — compiler and LLVM toolchain, runtime, kernel authoring frameworks and libraries, developer tooling, and deep PyTorch integration — and we co-design it with the silicon teams generation over generation.Within that stack, the AI kernel and optimization software development team drives the layer where architecture meets arithmetic. Our mission is performance \*and\* programmability at scale: hit roofline enablements on the workloads that matter, and make kernel authoring accessible enough that the whole organization can close coverage gaps without funneling every problem through a handful of experts. We do this by shipping high-performance kernel libraries with broad PyTorch operator coverage, by building the C++ and Python kernel authoring frameworks and DSL surfaces that others build on, and by writing production kernels against new architectures long before first silicon — turning hardware proposals into measured roofline evidence while the design can still change.We are hiring an experienced kernel and performance engineer to take on this role at a senior level. You will own the performance of workloads that serve billions of people, from the innermost loop of a fused attention kernel to the numeric decisions that determine whether a model converges. You will read hardware specifications and RTL-adjacent documentation as easily as you read code, and you will be expected to say clearly when the hardware — not the software — is the problem. Your findings will change what gets built next.This is a hands-on engineering role with wide latitude. The problems aren't incremental.## What you'll work on- \*\*Roofline-level kernels.\*\* GEMM and attention variants, normalization, collectives, elementwise and reduction fusions, sparse and quantized paths — implemented against novel architectural features (matrix engines, on-chip reduction fabrics, software-managed memory hierarchies) and tuned until the remaining gap to the machine's limit is explainable in a sentence.- \*\*Numerics under precision constraints.\*\* Low-precision formats (FP8, MX-style block-scaled types, integer quantization) where the difference between a correct scale choice and a plausible one is several decibels of signal, and where the fix has to work on silicon that has already been taped out.- \*\*Kernel authoring frameworks.\*\* Templateized, composable C++ kernel SDKs in the spirit of CUTLASS, Python DSLs in the spirit of Triton and CuTe, and the compiler-facing interfaces that let automated codegen reach performance that used to require a specialist.- \*\*Pre-silicon and bring-up.\*\* Kernels on simulators and emulators, validating architectural features and rooflines before tapeout, then first-light bring-up on real parts.- \*\*Software mitigations for hardware realities.\*\* Every chip ships with something you wish were different. Finding the workaround that recovers most of the lost performance — and generalizing it so nobody rediscovers it — is core to the job.  
  
  

### **Software Engineer, AI Kernels & Performance Optimization — MTIA Software Responsibilities:**

* Design, implement, and optimize high-performance compute and communication kernels for MTIA accelerators, taking ownership from architectural analysis through production deployment
* Profile and root-cause performance across the full stack — instruction scheduling, memory hierarchy and DMA behavior, on-chip interconnect, multi-device collectives — and drive the fixes to the right layer, whether that is the kernel, the compiler, the runtime, or the hardware
* Build and extend kernel authoring frameworks, templates, and libraries so that other engineers can reach high performance without deep architectural expertise
* raise the ceiling and lower the floor at the same time
* Deliver and maintain broad kernel coverage for PyTorch operators across recommendation, ranking, and generative AI workloads, in both eager and compiled execution paths
* Partner with silicon architecture and design teams on hardware/software co-design: quantify the value of proposed features with real kernels, characterize rooflines pre-silicon, and advocate for the changes the software stack actually needs
* Work with compiler, runtime, framework, and product-facing teams to land end-to-end wins on production models rather than isolated microbenchmark improvements
* Investigate numerics and precision trade-offs, and design software mitigations that recover performance or accuracy lost to hardware limitations
* Set technical direction for a kernel domain, write the design documents that align cross-functional partners, and mentor engineers on performance methodology and accelerator programming

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* Proficiency in C++ and Python, including low-level systems programming, templates and generic programming, and comfort reading and writing performance-critical code
* Demonstrated experience writing and optimizing kernels for a parallel architecture — GPU (CUDA, ROCm/HIP, SYCL/OpenCL), TPU or other AI ASICs, or SIMD/vector CPU targets
* Working knowledge of computer architecture as it applies to performance: memory hierarchies and bandwidth, latency hiding, occupancy and scheduling, vectorization, and synchronization

jobs.title: Embedded Flight Software Engineer (Early Career)
jobs.description:
York Space Systems was founded to radically improve spacecraft affordability and reliability, transforming, and enabling next- generation space mission operations worldwide. Today, York is one of the most innovative aerospace companies, specializing in end-to-end customer solutions and the rapid production of spacecraft platforms. York’s complete Space Segment Solution includes spacecraft production, payload integration, system integration & test, launch services, ground segment services, and mission operations, enabling customers to leverage York’s existing technology solutions to get to orbit rapidly and responsively. We’re looking to expand our team across the board.
  
  
York is seeking an early career Embedded Flight Software Engineer to support the design, development, integration, and testing of mission-critical spacecraft software systems. This role focuses on embedded and Linux-based flight software that enables command, telemetry, networking, and autonomy functions across on-orbit vehicles.
  
The ideal candidate is a motivated engineer who enjoys hands-on problem solving, learning complex systems, and working closely with multidisciplinary teams throughout development, integration, and test activities.
  
York operates in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment where engineers are trusted with meaningful responsibility early. High performers are given opportunities to grow quickly, influence technical direction, and contribute directly to on-orbit mission success.
  
  
Not all skills below are required — we encourage you to apply if you are excited about learning and growing in the role.
  
  
**Responsibilities:**  

* Support development of embedded flight software in C/C++ for spacecraft systems
* Assist with software integration and testing in HITL, flat-sat, and lab environments
* Help develop and maintain networking and communication interfaces between spacecraft subsystems and ground systems
* Participate in unit, integration, and system-level testing activities
* Support debugging of hardware/software integration issues
* Assist with on-orbit operations support and anomaly investigations
* Contribute to software documentation, interface definitions, and test procedures
* Work with CI/CD pipelines, build systems, and release processes
* Collaborate with software, hardware, platform, and mission operations teams
* Fast-paced environment with significant opportunities for career and technical growth based on performance and initiative

Required Qualifications
  

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related field
* 0–5 years of experience in software or embedded systems development
* Familiarity with C/C++ programming
* Exposure to Linux development environments
* Understand code and source repository management
* Basic understanding of networking concepts (TCP/IP, UDP, sockets, etc.)
* Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
* Ability to work in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment
* Must be clearance eligible and able to maintain an active Secret Clearance or higher
* Willingness to work full-time in our Greenwood Village, CO office
* Love space!

Preferred for the Role
  

* Master’s Degree in computer science or engineering related field
* Internship, academic, or personal project experience with embedded systems
* Familiarity with embedded Linux or Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS)
* Experience with hardware/software integration or robotics projects
* Exposure to Git, CI/CD pipelines, or automated testing
* Familiarity with Python or scripting languages
* Interest in spacecraft, aerospace, or safety-critical systems
* Experience working in lab or system integration environments
* Active Secret Clearance

In compliance with local law, we are disclosing the compensation, or a range thereof, for roles in locations where legally required. Actual salaries will vary based on several factors, including but not limited to external market data, internal equity, location, skill set, experience, and/or performance.
  
  
Benefits
  

* 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance (subject to spousal surcharge).
* Company holidays, floating holidays, and sick time.
* Unlimited PTO.
* Generous 401(k) match.

How To Apply
  
Interested candidates are encouraged to apply by clicking the “Apply” link at the top of the page. York Space Systems will be accepting applications on a rolling basis until the position is closed. York Space Systems provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, military or protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. Must have permanent authorization to work in the United States. This policy applies to all terms and conditions or employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training. jobs.title: Lead Systems Engineer-Terestrial Quantum Gravity Gradiometer (QGG)
jobs.description:
Infleqtion is a global quantum technology company solving the world’s most challenging problems. The company harnesses quantum mechanics to build and integrate quantum computers, sensors, and networks. From fundamental physics to leading edge commercial products, Infleqtion enables “quantum everywhere” through our ecosystem of devices and platforms.

We are seeking a technically exceptional and mission-driven Lead Systems Engineer to lead the end-to-end technical execution of a cutting-edge terrestrial gravity sensing development and productization program. As the technical authority, you will ensure that all engineering activities align with mission objectives, meet customer requirements, and integrate effectively across disciplines. The LSE will partner with project and portfolio leadership and help build a capable R&D and productization team with the mission of deploying quantum gravity and gravity gradiometer sensors in diverse terrestrial environments, including subsurface, surface, and airborne vehicles.

Job Responsibilities

The duties and responsibilities outlined below include essential functions of the role. Depending on business needs, this role may perform a combination of some or all the following duties. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned.

* Serve as the ultimate technical authority for the program, owning the end-to-end system design and architecture.
* Make final decisions on key trade-offs, technical issues, and risk mitigations.
* Growing a team and mentoring junior engineers and ICs with diverse skillsets across systems, mechanical, thermal, opto-mechanical, electrical, embedded control systems, and software.
* Coordinate and collaborate with quantum sensing subject matter experts to convert neutral atom sensing modalities into realizable, deployable, and higher performing mobile quantum gravity sensors
* Foster a collaborative and high-performance engineering culture.

* Work closely with the Program Manager to ensure technical execution supports cost and schedule objectives.
* Support ECP development, design-to-cost efforts, EAC reviews, and strategic technology roadmapping.
* Ensure the system is technically ready for major test campaigns and mission use.
* Identify, own, and drive resolution of high-impact technical risks and issues.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions for anomalies and failures.
* Champion technical excellence and rigorous engineering processes. Utilize experience during program execution to support continuous improvement of company engineering principles, practices, and procedures.
* Communicate technical progress, risks, and trade studies with transparency and confidence.

  
**Requirements**  

* Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, Physics, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications

* Master’s or Ph.D. in a relevant technical field.
* Prior experience as a technical expert on developmental deployed sensing systems, particularly in RF, EO/IR, or related missions.

jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Application deadline: Oct 12, 2026  
  
Join AWS Hardware Engineering to design the servers powering the world's leading cloud platform and AI/ML infrastructure. We're seeking an exceptional Linux Kernel Engineer to accelerate critical kernel initiatives across millions of servers worldwide.  
  
We are seeking an exceptional Linux Kernel Engineer to join our server firmware team. In this role, you will lead Linux kernel patching, code development, and version adoption for our server management controllers across a massive global fleet. You will ensure our kernel remains current, secure, and compliant with strict patching service-level agreements that directly impact AWS infrastructure reliability. Your work will power the backbone of AWS compute infrastructure, including the servers that enable AI/ML workloads for customers worldwide.  
  
The ideal candidate will be an innovative self-starter with deep expertise in Linux kernel internals, device driver development, and embedded Linux systems. You will gain comprehensive understanding of our server firmware kernel stack and analyze it in both current and future contexts. Using your systems knowledge, you will architect solutions to complex multi-factor problems, including kernel upgrade strategies that minimize customer impact, address security vulnerabilities rapidly, and optimize operational efficiency across millions of servers supporting diverse workloads from traditional compute to advanced machine learning applications.  
  
You will collaborate with engineers across AWS and external partners, leading development efforts that span kernel security, hardware enablement, and platform services teams. Your work will directly contribute to critical initiatives that keep our infrastructure patched, secure, and operationally excellent—ensuring the foundation for tomorrow's AI/ML innovations remains robust and scalable.  
  
AWS Engineers are shaping the way people use computers and designing the future of cloud computing technology – come help us make history!  
  
Key job responsibilities  
Design and develop firmware solutions for AWS servers, contributing to server designs that power millions of customer workloads.  
Lead the complete development lifecycle from initial conception through production deployment, ensuring robust and scalable firmware implementations across our massive server fleet.  
Architect and implement firmware deployment strategies that minimize customer impact while maintaining the highest standards of security and operational excellence.  
Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams including hardware engineers, validation teams, software services to optimize functionality and performance.  
Explore and evaluate emerging technologies and their potential impact on AWS infrastructure, making recommendations for adoption and integration into our firmware stack.  
Drive technical solutions for problems, balancing security requirements, operational efficiency, and system reliability.  
Tailor firmware solutions specifically for the AWS environment, ensuring seamless integration with our unique infrastructure requirements and operational workflows.  
Mentor team members and contribute to the continuous improvement of development processes, tools, and best practices.  
  
A day in the life  
Most mornings, you'll dive into code—whether that's developing new security features, optimizing firmware deployment strategies, or debugging a tricky issue that's affecting a subset of servers.  
You'll collaborate a lot. Maybe it's a quick sync with platform teams about an upcoming deployment, or a deeper technical discussion with hardware engineers about a new server design. You might work with internal customers to understand their requirements.

* Collaborate with the Systems Architecture and FSW teams on new component development
* Collaborate with other teams on simulation health
* Support internal users directly and incorporate their feedback into the simulation models

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

**Technical Execution**

* Build and ship full-stack applications end to end — data model, services and APIs, workflow, and web user interface — and operate them in production.

* Plan and execute migrations from off-the-shelf tools to in-house software: data migration, parallel operation, and cutover, without breaking traceability.

* Build in observability, auditability, sync health, and data-quality checks as first-class features.

* Set and uphold engineering standards — code quality, testing, reviews, and technical documentation.

**Leadership & Collaboration**

* Mentor senior and early-career engineers and raise the technical bar across the team.

* Work directly with engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing users to understand real workflows and ship software that fits them.

* Partner with the teams that own today's engineering and business systems to design integrations and plan migrations that respect how those systems are run.

* Experience building user-facing web applications end to end — from data model and APIs to a modern front end (e.g., TypeScript, React).

* Deep experience with API design, event-driven architectures, and reliably moving and transforming data between disparate systems.

* Strong grasp of domain data modeling for complex, versioned records, and of keeping data consistent and traceable across multiple systems of record.

* Experience building for observability, auditability, and data quality in production.

* Cloud and infrastructure fluency (e.g., AWS), plus strong fundamentals across networking, security, and CI/CD.

* Proficiency in one or more modern programming languages (e.g., Go, Python).

* Track record setting technical direction across multiple services or teams and mentoring other engineers, including senior engineers.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience building, extending, or integrating PLM, ERP, manufacturing execution (MES), requirements/ALM, or MBSE systems.

* Experience migrating an organization from an off-the-shelf system to in-house software, including data migration and user adoption.

* Strong product sense and experience working directly with engineering, manufacturing, or operations users.

* Familiarity with digital thread / digital engineering concepts and product-lifecycle data.

* Experience with Go and building products from an early stage.

* Familiarity with infrast

jobs.title: Robotics Software Engineer
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

The Robotics Software Engineer develops and maintains software for GPSI autonomous underwater vehicle systems. The position supports a ROS2-based software stack running on embedded Linux, with responsibilities spanning navigation, state estimation, sensor integration, deployment infrastructure, autonomy, and mission software. The role works across software and hardware boundaries and supports development through in-water testing and field deployment.

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s or master’s degree in robotics, computer science, engineering, or a related field.
* One to seven years of professional experience, or equivalent graduate research, working with physical robotic systems.
* Professional or research experience developing software in C++ and Python within a ROS or ROS2 environment.
* Experience working with embedded Linux and debugging software-to-hardware interfaces.
* **Must be a United States citizen.**

**Primary Job Duties**

**Navigation & State Estimation:**

* Develop, evaluate, and maintain algorithms for sensor fusion and coordinate-frame management across a multi-sensor suite operating in GPS-denied environments.
* Support evaluation and troubleshooting of navigation, state-estimation, and controls behavior using test data and physical vehicle results.

**Sensor Integration:**

* Develop and maintain driver-level software for vehicle sensors and embedded communication interfaces.
* Diagnose integration issues across application software, operating-system services, firmware interfaces, and connected hardware.
* Collaborate with cross-domain personnel to incorporate physical design changes and new sensors into the software stack.

**Systems & Infrastructure:**

* Build and maintain development and deployment tooling for a multi-vehicle fleet, including build pipelines, containerized development environments, device provisioning, and process management on embedded targets.
* Support repeatable software configuration, deployment, and troubleshooting across development and fielded systems.

**Autonomy & Mission Software:**

* Contribute to higher-level software governing mission execution, vehicle safety protocols, and communication with operators.
* Support autonomy architectures, mission planning, simulation, and vehicle-behavior testing as assigned.

**Required Knowledge and Skills**

* Proficiency in C++ and Python in a ROS or ROS2 environment.
* Firm grasp of state estimation, sensor fusion, or controls and the ability to reason about system behavior from first principles.
* Experience working with embedded Linux and comfort operating at the OS level.
* Ability to debug problems that cross abstraction layers, from algorithms to hardware communication.
* Self-directed and comfortable working in a small team with significant individual responsibility.
* Clear technical communication and documentation skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with marine, underwater, or field robotics.
* Familiarity with inertial navigation, acoustic sensing, or subsea communication systems.
* Experience with simulation frameworks for robotic vehicles.
* Background in autonomy architectures, behavior trees, or mission-planning systems.
* Experience with cross-compilation, containerized workflows, or CI/CD for embedded targets.

**Physical Demands and Work Environment**

This role involves extended periods of computer-based work in an office or engineering-lab environment and may include work around electronic equipment, autonomous underwater vehicles, test fixtures, docks, boats, or waterfront test locations. The position may require occasional lifting of equipment or materials weighing up to 25 pounds and participation in field or in-water test activities. Reasonable accommodation may be made as required.

Pay: $110,000.00 - $150,000.00 per year

### **Position Description & Qualifications**

  
  

Serco seeks a **Simulation Systems and Test Engineer** for its Combat Air Force Distributed Mission Operations (CAF DMO) 3.0 program in Orlando, FL. The CAF DMO 3.0 program, via its Distributed Mission Operations Network (DMON), provides world-class integration training in large force and small team formats to combat units around the globe against cutting-edge threats in a boundless virtual battlespace. The U.S. Air Force can only utilize its full capability against modern threats in a virtual environment. Be a part of that environment and continue to make the USAF the best air force in the world.

You will be part of a focused team of engineers to perform test, integration, and evaluation of disparate M&S systems and applications to support 5th and 6th generation training interoperability.

The team will work closely with the DoD customer and other Serco teams at Langley AFB and Orlando, FL to deliver quality test services.

**In this role, you will:**

* Support military simulation system and application integration, evaluation, and interoperability test to support DMON and JSE training operations.
* Use industry-standard tools for simulation test and evaluation to include Wireshark, simulation protocol analysis, and GFE and Commercial Computer Generated Forces (CGFs).
* Assist in detailed analysis of network and computational system performance including latency, bandwidth, jitter, and system occupancy measures.
* Help develop and maintain test plans and procedures to document and drive test activities.
* Draft comprehensive test reports based on completed integration, test, evaluation, and verification tasks performed.
* Assist in the development of CONOPS and multiple COAs for implementation and deployment of the evaluated simulation capabilities.
* Contribute to other areas of the engineering life cycle to include requirements review and assessment, training operations support, and basic system administration functions.
* Produce well-defined, concise, and directed test procedures and test cases under the guidance of senior engineers.
* Support program and team processes by using tools from the Atlassian Suite of products to include JIRA, Confluence, Bitbucket, Bamboo, and X-Ray.
* Participate in peer reviews, test bed maintenance and updates, and programming, testing, and debugging activities.
* Write and maintain scripts and support application (PowerShell, Cygwin, VBasic, etc.) programs, to enable efficiencies in test artifact creation and task execution.
* Help identify production and non-production application issues, assist in developing solutions, and implement necessary changes.

  

**To be successful in this role, you will have:**

* A bachelor’s degree in an applicable STEM curriculum (e.g., Data Analysis, System Engineering, Math, Computer Science, Physics, etc.) or similar.
* 8 years of engineering experience performing test, integration, SW development, or embedded systems engineering activities.
* Experience with military simulation integration test DIS IEEE1278.1 or HLA IEEE 1516 protocols, or similar communications or data protocols (SIP, VOIP, JREAP, etc).

* The ability to obtain a TS/SCI and SAP/SAR.

* Experience supporting DoD customers and personnel in a technical capacity.
* Familiarity or experience with development, test and evaluation of military simulation training or operational systems.
* Must possess, or obtain within six months, a DoD 8140 IAT Level II or higher (i.e. Security+, CySA+, CISSP)
* Up to 10% travel

  

**This position is contingent upon your ability to obtain/maintain/transfer your Secret clearance.**

**Additional desired experience and skills:**

* An active DoD Secret Clearance with ability to obtain TS/SCI and SAP/SAR.
* Familiarity with tactical Military training systems, products, and capabilities.
* Exposure to or experience in M&S development, test, and integration for constructive simulation systems and models.
* Knowledge of or experience with the Joint Simulation Environment (JSE).
* Possess or obtain within six months, a Linux OS certification (i.e., Linux+, RHCSA etc.).
  

  

### **Company Overview**

  
  

Serco Inc. (Serco) is the Americas division of Serco Group, plc. jobs.title: Mechanical Design Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
Chromalloy is a global engineering & solutions company. We are a leading provider of aftermarket parts, repairs, and solutions that safely & reliably extend the life of aircraft engines and gas turbines. We develop, manufacture and repair critical turbine components for a range of engine platforms. Our solutions support the engines running the aerospace, energy and defense industries around the world.
  
**Video:** What We Do
  
Why work at Chromalloy?
  
Chromalloy employees are proud, passionate problem-solvers who strive to live our values every day. A career with Chromalloy is an opportunity to learn from top industry experts, work with important technologies, and unlock a passion for innovation. Join our team of experts, innovators and problem-solvers delivering world-class solutions for our customers. As a global company, we are committed to creating an inclusive environment where all employees feel represented, heard, and able to bring their best selves to work every day. Be part of something bigger with Chromalloy!
  
Our Total Rewards Program is designed to support you today and in the future.
  

* Comprehensive and flexible benefit options starting on day one, including medical, dental, vision, EAP, wellness incentives, and 401(k) with employer matching.
* Development & progression opportunities for every employee – regular performance conversations, training and development curriculum, and engineering fellowship programs.
* Paid time off, including vacation, sick time, paid holidays, and parental leave—all eligible on your first day of employment!
* Competitive pay, including eligibility for quarterly and annual bonuses, depending on role and site.

Eligibility for individual benefit plans may vary based on employment status.
  
  
Job Summary
  
We’re looking for a Mechanical Design Automation Engineer to help design, deploy, and continuously improve robotic automation solutions across Chromalloy’s global manufacturing network. You’ll create practical, production-ready systems that strengthen safety, quality, productivity, and process consistency in critical aerospace manufacturing and repair operations.
  
  
Work That Matter
  
  
At Chromalloy, your work directly supports aviation safety and reliability. Our teams repair and manufacture critical aerospace components used across the global aviation industry. Whether you're improving processes, supporting operations, solving technical challenges, or driving business performance, your contributions help keep aircraft flying safely around the world.
  
  
**Location:** Oldsmar, FL
  
  
**Travel:** Up to 25% as needed
  
  
**Schedule:** On-site
  
  
What You’ll Be Doing
  
  
Support the mechanical design and development of robotic automation cells for aerospace manufacturing and repair operations.
  
  
Develop work cell layouts, robotic end-of-arm tooling (EOAT), fixtures, part presentation systems, safety guarding, and process-specific tooling.
  
  
Perform concept development, feasibility studies, design reviews, and risk assessments for new automation opportunities.
  
  
Create detailed 3D models, mechanical drawings, assemblies, and technical documentation using CAD software.
  
  
Design flexible, reusable tooling and automation concepts that can be deployed across multiple facilities.
  
  
Partner with manufacturing and production teams to automate welding, inspection, masking, blending, material handling, surface preparation, and other processes.
  
  
Troubleshoot mechanical and process-related issues during equipment integration, implementation, and startup.
  
  
Support ergonomic evaluations, machine safety reviews, system validation, and process qualification activities.
  
  
Contribute to automation design standards, best practices, and reusable system architectures.
  
  
What We’re Looking For
  
  
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  
  
Experience designing robotic work cells from concept through production deployment.
  
  
Advanced proficiency in 3D CAD software; Siemens NX is preferred.
  
  
Strong knowledge of automation, control systems, robotics principles, and robotic work cell design.
  
  
Experience designing robotic tooling and EOAT, automation fixtures, part handling systems, safety guarding, or automated manufacturing equipment.
  
  
Understanding of GD&T, tolerance stack-up analysis, and Design for Manufacturing (DFM).
  
  
Familiarity with industrial robotics platforms, machine vision, laser systems, sensors, and industrial automation equipment.
  
  
Knowledge of machine safety standards and risk assessment methodologies.
  
  
Experience working directly with manufacturing operations and production teams.
  
  
Strong communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently across multiple sites and shifting priorities.
  
  
Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% to support automation builds and deployments.
  
  
Nice to Have
  
  
Experience with aerospace manufacturing or repair operations.
  
  
Knowledge of FANUC or ABB robotic platforms.
  
  
Experience automating welding, coating, inspection, machining, or material finishing processes.
  
  
Experience with additive manufacturing design principles.
  
  
Exposure to PLCs, HMI systems, industrial networking, and controls integration.
  
  
Experience with simulation software, offline robotic programming, or digital twin development.
  
  
Experience using AI tools to accelerate work.
  
  
Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma exposure.
  
  
Physical Requirements
  
  
Work in a production floor environment with ventilation, climate control, moderate lighting, and moderate noise.
  
  
Use finger dexterity to type, adjust, move, handle, operate, install, attach, remove, apply, grasp, manipulate, and measure.
  
  
Occasionally move, transport, rotate, reach, pull, twist, adjust position,

jobs.title: Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. The Reliability & Maintenance Engineering (RME) team are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the robotics and material handling equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey!  
  
About the Role:  
As an Automation Engineer, you will play a crucial role in maximizing equipment reliability and operational performance in our fulfillment centers by providing proactive controls automation and technical support. Your expertise will be essential in troubleshooting complex control systems, analyzing performance metrics, and driving continuous improvement initiatives. You'll collaborate with cross-functional teams to optimize material handling equipment (MHE) systems and implement innovative projects. You'll work with state-of-the-art technology, including conveyors, sortation systems, scanners, cameras, print and apply systems, and SCADA devices and programs. Through your efforts, you'll directly contribute to ensuring our customers receive their orders with Amazon's signature speed and accuracy.  
  
What Do We Offer?  
Amazon offers competitive compensation packages including comprehensive healthcare benefits starting on Day 1, matching 401(k) program, and up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave. But wait, there’s more: We provide lightweight fire-resistant daily wear and composite toe safety shoes for your safety!  
  
Key job responsibilities  
Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:  

* You will serve as the site expert for maintaining the automation systems that are critical for operations
* You will understand, maintain and troubleshoot material handling control systems, including PLC/PC controllers and industrial networks such as Ethernet, ControlNet, DeviceNet, Profibus, motor control systems, servo drives, frequency drives, and electrical distribution systems
* You will monitor MHE metrics and partner with maintenance/operations to address system performance issues and provide analysis across all operations
* You will provide first-level escalation support for site technicians, both locally and remotely
* You will perform and analyze building System Assessments to enhance material handling system performance

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, automation engineering, or equivalent, or 2+ years of PLC programming or automation engineering experience
* Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
* Bachelor's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, automation engineering, or equivalent, or 2+ years of process or production environment related PLC-controlled automation and issue diagnosis experience
* Bachelor's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, automation engineering, or equivalent, or 2+ years of robotics work cells and control systems experience
* Bachelor's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, automation engineering, or equivalent, or 2+ years of electrical theory, robotics, controls components, and automated equipment experience
* Bachelor's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, automation engineering, or equivalent, or 2+ years of Ladder Logic and structured programming from Siemens, Allen-Bradley, or Codesys PLCs experience

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* Experience with HMI and control network components, including maintenance, troubleshooting, programming and design
* Experience identifying, maintaining, troubleshooting, and modifying Motor Controls including motor starters, Variable Frequency Drives, DC drives, and standard electrical components
* Experience with preventive maintenance procedures, industrial electrical, industrial controls, and industrial electronics & robotics
* Experience interpreting and modifying mechanical and electrical drawings
* Experience programming with RSLogix5000, Studio 5000, FT View, and other controls software platforms

  
Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.  
  
Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. jobs.description:
At Boeing, we innovate and collaborate to make the world a better place. We’re committed to fostering an environment for every teammate that’s welcoming, respectful and inclusive, with great opportunity for professional growth. Find your future with us.

The Boeing Defense (BDS), Security, Space, Intelligence & Weapons Systems (SI&WS) is seeking multiple **Senior Systems Engineers** to join our Experimental Systems Group (ESG) at **Kennedy Space Center, FL**.

At Boeing, our Systems Engineers drive the innovation, development, evaluation, and end-to-end execution of validation methods and test systems across manufacturing, refurbishment, integrated vehicle testing, and operational checkout. In this role, you will operate across multiple engineering disciplines to verify system-of-systems performance, serving as the technical bridge between design intent, physical hardware validation, and flight readiness through the following responsibilities.

**Position Responsibilities:**

* Define, decompose, and coordinate system-level test and verification requirements derived from customer, mission, and operational needs
* Integrate cross-functional parameters across electrical, mechanical, fluids, thermal, and software interfaces to verify end-to-end compatibility and functional integrity
* Lead specialized analyses including safety, reliability, maintainability, testability, survivability, and requirement certification to optimize configurations for mission success
* Govern requirements management and verification tracking using formal tools, risk/opportunity frameworks, and readiness assessments to ensure complete verification closure

* Represent the system test organization directly in the factory, test cell, and post-production environments throughout hardware builds, integrated functional testing, and refurbishment cycles
* Lead dynamic system test operations, translating complex flight and ground environments into actionable test procedures, instrumentation strategies, and acceptance criteria
* Author technical dispositions and engineering deviations for hardware non-conformances, operational limit exceedances, or test anomalies to maintain operational cadence without sacrificing safety or quality

* Lead rapid root-cause analysis (RCA), failure investigation, and multi-system troubleshooting to diagnose complex operational anomalies and flight hardware defects
* Identify, develop, and deploy continuous upgrades to test infrastructure, instrumentation setups, and operational processes to improve test cadence, reliability, and mission throughput

**Basic Qualifications (Required Skills/Experience):**

* Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology (including Manufacturing Technology), Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry or non-US equivalent qualifications directly related to the work statement
* Active U.S. Top Secret / SCI security clearance (investigation active or open within the past 24 months; U.S. citizenship required)
* 7+ years of experience in an engineering role
* Ability to analyze and interpret engineering drawings, schematics, wiring diagrams, and parts lists
* Strong skills in engineering analysis, requirements tracing, and technical communication

**Preferred Qualifications (Desired Skills/Experience):**

* Expertise in system-level tests and verification of space vehicles or space systems
* Refined cross-functional leadership skills and experience working with multi-disciplined teams
* Expert in aerospace avionics, electrical systems, and RF equipment
* Subject matter expert for approved repair and testing techniques for electronics and components
* Experience with hardware and software requirements verification using tools like DOORS
* Scripting experience for test automation or data processing (e.g., Python, Tcl/Tk, Perl)
* Experience with configuration management and tracking tools (e.g., Git, SVN, PLM, Jira, MS Project)

**Conflict of Interest:**

Successful candidates for this job must satisfy the Company’s Conflict of Interest (COI) assessment process.

Boeing is a Drug Free Workplace where post offer applicants and employees are subject to testing for marijuana, cocaine, opioids, amphetamines, PCP, and alcohol when criteria is met as outlined in our policies*.*

jobs.title: Instrumentation & Controls Engineer I
jobs.description:
At Relativity Space, we're building rockets to serve today's needs and tomorrow's breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that's just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven't been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you're in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you'll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we're writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it's early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

**About the Team:**

The Launch team operates at the intersection of every major aspect of Terran R, from stages and payloads to ground systems, launch, landing, and refurbishment. The Cape is the only place where you see it all come together, offering a level of exposure and responsibility unmatched elsewhere in the program. This is where first flights happen, where history is built on top of history, and where the scale of what's underway is unlike anything in modern aerospace. The mission stays the same, but the work evolves with every milestone: from first launch to reuse, high-cadence operations, and beyond. If you're looking to define what's next in space launch and write a new playbook, not just repeat what's already been done, this is where it happens.

**About the Role:**

* Design, develop, test, integrate, and operate launch control and acquisition hardware, instrumentation, and cameras used to support and control the Terran R rocket.
* Work with Beckhoff PLCs or similar systems.
* Support high-speed data acquisition.
* Work with instrumentation including pressure, temperature, flow, level, accelerometers, solenoid valves, VFDs, and heaters.
* Integrate and operate IP, SDI, and CoaXPress high-speed cameras.
* Assist in the design of electrical systems for use in hazardous areas.
* Collaborate with other groups to gather requirements, plan schedules, and coordinate work.
* Plan, install, and operate wiring and hardware in access-limited areas such as launch mounts and transport erectors.

**About You:**

* Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or another related STEM discipline.
* Exposure to data acquisition hardware, PLC-based control systems, complex camera systems, and instrumentation selection and troubleshooting.
* Ability to work with multidisciplinary groups in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

**Nice to haves but not required:**

* Experience with the design and operation of spacecraft and launch vehicle infrastructure.
* Experience working at a rocket launch site.
* Proficiency with electrical schematic design software such as AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN, or Zuken E3.

**Successful candidates must clear a background check administered by the US government to obtain clearance for on-site work at our government partner location in Cape Canaveral, Florida.**

**We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.**

***If you need a reasonable accommodation, please contact us at*** ***accommodations@relativityspace.com******.***

***Please note: Relativity Space does not accept unsolicited resumes, candidate profiles, or referrals from recruitment agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited submission - via email, our website, social media, or directly to an employee - will be deemed the property of Relativity Space, and no fee will be owed absent a current, fully executed agreement with Talent Acquisition that specifically authorizes submissions for the applicable role.***

----------------------------

Space is a critical domain, connecting our technologies, our security and our humanity. While others view space as a destination, we see it as a realm of possibilities, where we can do more — we can innovate, invest, inspire and integrate our capabilities to transform the future.

At Lockheed Martin Space, we aim to harness the full potential of space to cultivate innovation, reduce costs, and push the boundaries of what technology can achieve. We’re creating future-ready solutions, focusing on resiliency and urgency through our 21st Century Security® vision. We’re erasing boundaries and forming partnerships across industries and around the world. We’re advancing spacecraft and the workforce to fuel the next generation. And we’re reimagining how space can connect us, ensuring security and prosperity.

Join Our Team as an **Electrical Engineer** and become a member of the US Navy's Fleet Ballistic Missile (FBM) D5 Life Extension 2 (D5LE2) Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE team. This is an exciting opportunity to work on the Fleet Ballistic Missile Program (FBM), a 63-year-old Program with a long-standing history of Mission Success and of a strong partner can thrive in an exciting fast-paced dynamic environment?

**What does this role look like?**

The FBM Program is experiencing significant growth, and we need your expertise to deliver amazing new technologies to our customers while maintaining the technical requirements of the strategic deterrence.

The Electronics Engineer II is an individual contributor on the LE2 – EGSE team supporting the FBM program. You will design and integrate hardware for Automated Test Equipment (ATE). Work is performed under the direction of senior engineers and is focused on delivering hardware deliverables on schedule. This role blends electrical‑hardware design, system integration, and test‑equipment development in a fast‑paced, mission‑oriented environment.

* Review and/or Develop schematics, wiring diagrams for hardware modules.

**To be effective in this role, you will need:**  

* Experience in both design and test of electrical hardware
* 2+ years professional experience required for this role.
* You will need to obtain and maintain a DoD Top Secret Clearance, thus US Citizenship is required.

The information below reflects the standard job description for this position: Researches, designs, develops, and tests a variety of electronic equipment and systems, including radar and radiation detection equipment; radio, television and other communications equipment and systems; circuitry components; analog and digital computers; and control and test equipment.

* U.S. Citizenship (required for DoD Secret clearance)
* Prior professional experience in electrical hardware design and test
* Experience troubleshooting interactions between software and hardware such as network devices and lab instrumentation

**Desired Skills**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline from an accredited college or a related discipline or equivalent experience/combined education.
* Proficiency with Creo/Windchill, Zuken, Pspice, or comparable tools.
* Experience with cable design
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Experience with interconnect design, schematic development, system integration and hardware verification.
* Experience with product‑lifecycle management (Design, Development, Deployment) and issue‑tracking systems.
* Prior work on EGSE, or communications systems for aerospace/defense.
* Familiarity with Atlassian Products development processes.
* Proficient in AI prompting as it applies to this position and practice.

By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. We are seeking a Software Engineer to join our Command & Control team in Atlanta. The team is responsible for the design, development, integration, testing, and delivery of software supporting Human Machine Interfaces (HMI), Pilot Vehicle Interfaces (PVI), Command & Control (C2), telemetry, and vehicle communications.

This role will focus primarily on the embedded flight software and networking that enable communication between our aircraft and ground control systems. You will develop software supporting command and control, telemetry, network management, RF communications, and vehicle data links while working closely with avionics, RF, flight software, and ground systems engineers.

With safety at the forefront of our minds, our Atlanta factory proudly and passionately produces 460,000 tons a year of our dry pet food brands, including Alpo®, Beneful®, Cat Chow®, Dog Chow®, Friskies®, Purina ONE®, and Pro Plan®. jobs.description:
**About Carrier**

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure safe transport of food, lifesaving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do. For more information, visit corporate.carrier.com or follow on Carrier social media at @Carrier.

**About Automated Logic**

At Automated Logic, we've been developing and supporting intelligent building solutions that have helped customers, including small businesses to Fortune 500 corporations, operate their buildings more efficiently for over 40 years. Our products help reduce energy consumption, lower utility, operating and maintenance costs, and improve indoor air quality, occupant comfort, and productivity. Technology that supports the buildings and industry of today and tomorrow requires a wide range of talents and skill sets.

**About this role:**

As an Associate Controls Engineer, you will be crucial to ALC’s business through the designing of building automation systems created specifically for each individual customer. We are looking for someone who works well in a team and has excellent problem-solving, time management, and multi-tasking skills. You will work to build new skills and advance existing skills while completing smaller projects on your own.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Design and program building automation systems, site-specific configuration of control system, and control algorithms.
* Adhere to project requirements and company and customer standards of design, programming, and implementation.
* Create a clear design document for project teams with technical information.
* Document and communicate the building automation system design and revisions.
* Develop graphical and text-based interfaces for building automation systems.
* Test programming and interfaces prior to implementation.
* Provide technical support to sales representatives to ensure customers’ needs are met.
* Identify and communicate project opportunities and risks.
* Support functional testing for building systems.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Associate or Bachelor’s Degree

OR

* High School Diploma / GED with 2+ years of HVAC/BMS experience
* Must have unrestricted authorization to work in the USA. No visa sponsoring available.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Basic knowledge of primary functions of building automation system software and associated engineering tools, Automated Logic suites preferred.
* Basic knowledge of Automated Logic software, peripherals, add-ons, services, or hardware design.
* Understanding and/or experience with IP networks
* Understanding and/or experience with Microsoft Visio and/or similar software.
* Ability to understand written sequences of operations, diagrammatic depictions of systems.
* Familiar with third-party communication protocols used in building automation, such as BACnet, Modbus, SNMP, LON, N2, etc.
* Able to translate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
* Capable of climbing ladders or using other lift equipment over 8 feet above grade, and capable of lifting items up to 50lbs.

**Pay Range**

The annual salary for this position is between $53,000.00 - $106,000.00 annually. Factors which may affect pay within this range include, but are not limited to, skills, education, experience, and other unique qualifications of the successful candidate. The pay range will not be below the minimum wage applicable to the jurisdiction in which the applicant is to be employed.

**Other Compensation**

This position may be entitled to short-term cash incentives, subject to plan requirements.

**Benefits**

Employees are eligible for benefits, including:

* **Health Care Benefits**: Medical, Dental, Vision; Wellness incentives
* **Retirement Benefits**
* **Time off and Leave**: Paid vacation days, up to 15 days; paid sick days, up to 5 days; paid personal leave, up to 5 days; paid holidays, up to 13 days; birth and adoption leave; parental leave; family and medical leave; bereavement leave; jury duty leave; military leave; purchased vacation
* **Disability**: Short-term and long-term disability
* **Life Insurance and Accidental Death and Dismemberment**
* **Tax-Advantaged Accounts:** Health Savings Account; Health Care Spending Account; Dependent Care Spending Account
* **Tuition Assistance**

**Pay Range:**

$96,500.00 - $135,200.00

The actual annual salary offered to a candidate will be based on variables including experience, geographic location, education, and skills/achievements, and will be mutually agreed upon at the time of offer.

  

**Job Description**
===================

CCI/SPEER is seeking an **Electrical Controls Engineer** to join the team. In this role you will be responsible for developing, implementing, and supporting technology to improve equipment, processes, and products. This is accomplished through design requirements, specifications, drawings, procurement of necessary materials and services, and coordination of installation and training for systems including new automation solutions. You will provide expertise in programming and designing industrial controls and interfaces for new and existing equipment and processes. Effectively communicate with team members at all levels of the organization to improve our workplace, manufacturing performance, and customer experience.

This position may be filled at the Engineer I, II, or III level based on education, experience, and demonstrated technical capability. *Equivalent combinations of education, technical training, apprenticeship experience, licensure, military experience, certifications, and directly related controls/automation experience will be considered.*

This position reports to the Manufacturing Engineering Manager and will be based out of our **Lewiston, Idaho** office.

**What you'll do:**

* Support the design, development, implementation, and continuous improvement of automated manufacturing systems.

* Design, program, troubleshoot, and commission PLC-based control systems using platforms such as Allen-Bradley, Omron, or similar technologies.

* Develop and maintain HMI and operator interface systems to improve equipment usability and diagnostics.

* Assist with or lead automation projects involving robotics, vision systems, servo motion, industrial networking, and process controls based on experience level.

* Design, implement, maintain, and improve electrical instruments, equipment, facilities, and systems within the manufacturing environment.

* Participate in capital projects including concept development, design, procurement, installation, startup, and project validation.

* Troubleshoot equipment and process issues using a structured root cause problem-solving approach, identifying underlying causes rather than simply replacing components.

* Collaborate with operations, maintenance, engineering, quality, and IT teams to develop practical and scalable manufacturing solutions.

* Support integration of machine data into manufacturing and business systems for improved reporting, traceability, and decision making.

jobs.title: Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
If you thrive in fast paced environments, enjoy hands-on problem solving, and want to make a measurable impact while working with modern automation and control systems, this role offers the challenge, autonomy, and growth opportunities to take your engineering career to the next level.

In this role, you won’t just maintain systems—you’ll continuously improve them. You’ll apply your controls and automation knowledge to optimize preventive maintenance strategies, diagnose sophisticated issues, and enhance the performance of industry leading technologies such as conveyors, sortation systems, PLCs, scanners, vision systems, print

‑and

‑apply equipment, and SCADA platforms. Your work will directly influence uptime, safety, and operational excellence across mission critical facilities.

What You’ll Do

* Promote a safe working environment by complying with all applicable codes, regulations, governmental agencies, and company directives related to system operations and work safety.
* Troubleshoot and modify software programs for material handling control systems, including PLC/PC controllers, Allen Bradley Controllogix/Compactlogix PLC platform and RSLogix 5000 software package.
* Act as first level escalation in troubleshooting support, both on-site and remotely, as well as during and after business hours, to repair all MHE controls software systems. Respond quickly to emergency situations, summoning assistance as needed.
* Inspect systems to ensure the operation of equipment is within design capabilities and achieve operational conditions prescribed by the client.
* Oversee scope of development, work request initiation, scheduling, and inspection of work performed by outside contractors, which includes proprietary work, licensed installations, upgrades, and maintenance and inspection of specialized systems.
* Engineer process solutions and reliability improvement from concept to network implementation.
* Monitor Industrial networks such as Ethernet, ControlNet, DeviceNet, Profibus, AS-I, motor control systems, servo drives, frequency drives, and electrical distribution systems.
* Monitor material handling equipment metrics and partner with site team to resolve equipment electrical problems that create performance deficiencies.
* Proactively and effectively communicate with multiple stakeholders including, but not limited to, leadership, operations and the maintenance team on technical issues and project timelines and production impacts.
* Facilitate analysis and reviews of failures and processes to provide recommendations to implement improvements or retraining to avoid future incidents.
* Perform controls systems assessments to maintain and improve equipment reliability.
* Clearly communicate technical issues, project timelines, and product impacts with site leadership, operations and maintenance teams.
* Cultivate positive working relationships with our Client and the Operations Maintenance team members.
* Perform other job-related duties as needed or assigned.

What You’ll Need

* Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future.
* Bachelor's Degree preferred with 2-5 years of relevant experience. In lieu of a degree, a combination of experience and education may be considered.
* Experience in at least two engineering design cycles including specification, component selection and programming.
* 2+ years of experience working with PLC programming, robotics system components and controls, and SCADA-based monitoring and control systems.
* Ability to be available and work in a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays.
* Ability to independently solve problems and carry out general instructions in standard situations with limited to no oversight.
* Meet the physical requirements of this role including stooping, standing, walking, climbing stairs/ladders, and the ability to lift/carry heavy loads of 50 lbs. or more.
* Ability to guide the exchange of sensitive, complicated, and difficult information, convey performance expectations, and handle problems.

Preferred Qualifications

* 2+ years apprenticeship or equivalent experience in Control Systems troubleshooting/ programming.
* Experience supporting a range of different conveyors and sortation systems.
* Experience with robotic maintenance.
* In-depth knowledge of Microsoft Office products. Examples include Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.
* Extensive organizational skills with a strong inquisitive mindset.
* Advanced math skills. Ability to calculate difficult figures such as percentages, fractions, and other financial-related calculations.

You should be proficient in:

* PLC Programming Experience
* SCADA Experience

Machines & technologies you'll use:

* Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) (Allen Bradley)
